overall_summary: Bitcoin is under clear pressure as US-Iran strikes and a stronger dollar from multi-year high yields drag risk assets lower, with ETF outflows adding to the selloff near ten-day lows. Corporate buyers like Strategy, Capital B, and Remixpoint are still accumulating, but that support is overshadowed by hawkish Fed hike odds and escalating geopolitics. Near-term tone stays defensive into the remaining jobs data this week.
key_points: US-Iran strikes and Hormuz risk hit BTC
Yields and dollar surge; Fed hike odds jump
Strategy, Capital B, Remixpoint still buying BTC
Jobs data ahead keeps macro uncertainty elevated

items.title: US-Iran strikes send Bitcoin to 10-day lows near $76k
items.summary: Fresh US strikes on Iranian IRGC targets near the Strait of Hormuz, confirmed by CENTCOM and Trump, triggered a sharp risk-off move. Bitcoin fell through 78k and tested the mid-76k area while oil jumped above 90 to 95 dollars and Treasury yields spiked. Traders should care because the geopolitics are lifting inflation and rate-hike odds, pressuring risk assets and producing clustered long liquidations. Watch whether BTC holds current support or cascades lower if the conflict escalates further.
items.impact: Near-term risk-off pressure and higher volatility on BTC and alts

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs post $236M outflows after best August of 2026
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly 236 and a half million dollars in net outflows on September 1, the largest single day since late July, with BlackRock IBIT accounting for about 85 percent. This followed August’s strongest month of the year at around 3.5 billion dollars in inflows that pushed assets near 100 billion. Traders should watch this closely because ETF flows have been a primary price driver; a quick flip from heavy buying to selling can sap momentum just as September seasonality kicks in. Solana and some other crypto ETFs still saw inflows, pointing to rotation rather than a total exit.
items.impact: Weakens near-term institutional demand and adds selling pressure

items.title: Strategy CEO defends $60k sales, confirms 4,603 BTC buy at $80k
items.summary: Strategy CEO Phong Le told Bloomberg the firm sold Bitcoin near 60k earlier and then bought 4,603 BTC last week at an average of about 80,318 dollars because decisions track cost of capital, not spot price alone. Holdings now stand near 845,050 BTC and the company says it remains a net accumulator with a fortress balance sheet and near-zero net leverage on its metric. Traders care because Strategy is still the largest corporate holder; confirmation of resumed buying and no forced selling removes a key overhang. Le signaled more purchases are possible if equity issuance stays accretive.
items.impact: Supports corporate accumulation narrative and reduces sale fears

items.title: Bitcoin enters first hashrate bear market as miners pivot to AI
items.summary: Twenty One Capital CEO Raphael Zagury said Bitcoin is in its first true hashrate bear market, with network power down roughly 22 to 24 percent from the late-2025 peak and stuck below record for the longest stretch in a decade. Public miners are redirecting power and capital toward AI and high-performance computing instead of simply relocating machines as they did after the 2021 China ban. This matters for traders because lower hashrate can ease difficulty and boost remaining miners’ share, but it also raises longer-term questions about security budget and hashprice if the AI shift sticks. Difficulty has already adjusted lower in recent months.
items.impact: Structural mining shift; potential difficulty relief but security watch

items.title: Capital B raises €7.6M from Adam Back to buy more Bitcoin
items.summary: European Bitcoin treasury firm Capital B closed a 7.6 million euro private placement with Blockstream’s Adam Back, netting about 7.3 million euros after fees. Proceeds are earmarked mainly to add up to 376 BTC, which would lift holdings toward 3,521 coins, with warrants that could unlock far more capital later. This is another listed-company accumulation signal from a high-profile Bitcoin builder at a time when some corporates have turned more cautious. Traders should note the continued institutional and treasury demand for spot BTC even amid macro noise.
items.impact: Adds incremental corporate buying pressure and positive sentiment

items.title: Japan’s Remixpoint dumps alts, goes Bitcoin-only with 1,506 BTC
items.summary: Japan-listed Remixpoint sold its entire Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin stack on September 1 for roughly 879 million yen, booking about 118 million yen in profit, and now holds only around 1,506 Bitcoin. The firm cited market conditions, risk-return profiles and financial strategy, and has also earned lending yield on its BTC. This is a clean corporate vote of confidence in Bitcoin over alts and removes potential altcoin selling overhang from that balance sheet. It reinforces the treasury trend favoring BTC as the primary reserve asset.
items.impact: Positive for BTC dominance and corporate treasury narrative

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Hits Multi-Year High Near 4.82%
items.summary: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield surged to around 4.81-4.82 percent, its highest since late 2023, as oil prices spiked on renewed US-Iran strikes and global bond markets sold off. Higher yields raise borrowing costs across the economy and tighten financial conditions. Crypto traders should watch this closely because elevated rates and a stronger dollar typically pressure risk assets like Bitcoin in the near term.
items.impact: Higher yields and tighter conditions weigh on risk assets

items.title: Fed September Hike Odds Jump to About 66-68%
items.summary: Markets now price roughly a two-thirds chance of a 25-basis-point rate increase at the mid-September FOMC meeting, up sharply from under 40 percent a week earlier. This follows hawkish remarks from Chair Kevin Warsh and Governor Michael Barr warning that sticky inflation may require action, plus rising oil-driven price pressures. For crypto, a more hawkish Fed path raises the odds of tighter liquidity and higher opportunity costs for holding non-yielding assets.
items.impact: Increased rate-hike probability pressures risk appetite

items.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI Cools to 54.6 in August
items.summary: The ISM manufacturing index fell to 54.6 from 55.6, missing the 55.2 consensus but still signaling an eighth month of expansion. New orders slowed notably to 53.7 while the prices-paid index stayed elevated at 71.1, pointing to ongoing cost pressures from energy, tariffs, and supply issues. Traders care because softer activity could ease rate fears somewhat, yet sticky input prices keep the Fed cautious and support higher yields.
items.impact: Mixed growth signal with persistent inflation pressure

items.title: JOLTS Job Openings Rise to 7.271 Million in July
items.summary: Job openings increased to 7.271 million from a downwardly revised 7.182 million, missing expectations near 7.3 million, while hires and quits softened. The data shows a still-sturdy but cooling labor market with fewer voluntary separations. This is relevant ahead of Friday's payrolls because a gradual labor slowdown could temper Fed hike urgency, though it has not yet reversed the recent rise in rate expectations.
items.impact: Softening labor demand may modestly ease hike pressure

items.title: US Dollar Index Climbs Toward 99.8 on Yield Surge
items.summary: The DXY rose to around 99.7-99.8, near recent highs, supported by climbing Treasury yields and higher odds of a Fed rate hike. A stronger dollar often coincides with tighter global financial conditions and weaker commodity and crypto prices. Crypto traders should note the inverse correlation, as dollar strength can amplify selling pressure in risk-on assets during macro uncertainty.
items.impact: Stronger USD typically headwinds for Bitcoin and risk assets

items.title: Key Data Ahead: ADP Today, Beige Book, NFP Friday
items.summary: Markets await today's ADP private employment report for August, the Fed's Beige Book at 2pm ET, and Friday's nonfarm payrolls as critical inputs before the September FOMC. Soft labor prints could dial back hike bets while strong numbers or inflationary anecdotes would reinforce them. Crypto traders must stay nimble because these releases can rapidly shift rate expectations and dollar/yield moves that drive short-term Bitcoin volatility.
items.impact: Upcoming data will drive near-term rate and risk sentiment

items.title: US and Iran Exchange Fresh Strikes Near Hormuz
items.summary: The United States launched a new wave of airstrikes on IRGC targets in southern Iran near the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Iranian missile and drone retaliation against US bases in Jordan, Iraq, Bahrain and Kuwait. Oil jumped more than four dollars a barrel with Brent near ninety-five, as traffic through the critical chokepoint stays heavily disrupted. Traders should care because this is the biggest escalation in weeks, stoking inflation fears, higher yields and risk-off pressure across markets including crypto.
items.impact: Oil spike and risk-off hit equities and Bitcoin

items.title: European Gas Hits Three-Year High on Iran Fears
items.summary: Dutch TTF natural gas futures surged to their highest level since early 2023 as US-Iran fighting raised fresh worries about prolonged LNG disruptions from the Gulf. European storage sits well below seasonal norms heading into winter, amplifying the price spike. For traders this feeds directly into higher inflation expectations, bond sell-offs and tighter financial conditions that typically weigh on risk assets.
items.impact: Energy inflation pressures rates and risk appetite

items.title: Germany Blames Russia for Leipzig Airport Drone Attack
items.summary: Berlin formally attributed an August explosives-laden drone incident near Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig airport to Russian hybrid operations and ordered the closure of Moscow’s Bonn consulate plus a cultural centre. Interior Minister Dobrindt called Germany a daily target of hybrid warfare while Putin dismissed the claims as fabricated. This raises NATO-Europe tension risk and could tighten sanctions or defence spending that ripple into energy and risk markets.

items.title: China Blocks G20 Consensus on Trade Imbalances
items.summary: China alone rejected language at the US-hosted G20 finance ministers meeting calling for elimination of non-market policies that drive export surpluses and global imbalances. The other nineteen members backed a chair’s statement targeting those distortions, including energy and Hormuz concerns. Persistent US-China trade friction like this keeps tariff and supply-chain uncertainty high, which is rarely friendly for risk assets.
items.impact: Sustains trade-war overhang without new immediate shock

items.title: Putin Pledges Iran Support Amid Ukraine Strikes
items.summary: At the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, Putin told Iran’s president Moscow is supplying necessary goods and stands in full solidarity as the US-Iran fight continues. At the same time Russian forces launched heavy drone and missile attacks on Kyiv that killed at least a dozen people and targeted energy infrastructure. Dual-front support for adversaries of the West prolongs both conflicts and keeps energy and geopolitical risk elevated for markets.
items.impact: Prolongs dual energy and war risk premium

items.title: Chevron Expands Venezuela Oil Output Under US Deal
items.summary: Chevron announced more than seven billion dollars of investment to more than double its Venezuela production to roughly six hundred thousand barrels a day, adding Orinoco Belt acreage under improved terms. This follows a broader Trump administration push for US control of Venezuelan oilfields previously influenced by China and Russia after Maduro’s removal. Extra Western Hemisphere supply could eventually ease some oil tightness, though near-term geopolitics still dominate price action.
items.impact: Potential medium-term oil supply offset, limited immediate relief
